items.title: Group-like p-form global symmetry and backgrounds
items.design_state: Codimension-general topological-defect prerequisite is current and ready. Direct dependency corrected from the supplier codimension-one interface definition; owner escalation is recorded for this cross-batch edge change.
items.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge1$, an integer $p$ with $0\le p<d$, and a smooth $d$-dimensional spacetime manifold $M$, possibly with boundary. A selected model $\mathcal T$ specifies its spacetime structure and boundary conditions; field configuration space, field bundles, regularity and admitted sectors; observables and their supports; complete admissible insertion inputs, including decorated defects and networks, and their correlation functionals with an explicit normalization; and, when present, its action, regulator, measure, unit system and charge normalization. No such data are inferred from a familiar theory name.

Use the preceding topological-defect definition with its exact content: a defect is model-specified field, operator or boundary-condition data on a closed embedded support, and it is topological when every declared correlator is invariant under each admissible isotopy that transports its data, avoids other insertions and preserves boundary data. For this symmetry, each defect is an endodefect insertion in the same selected model; the model supplies parallel fusion and the induced action on its admitted observables and backgrounds. A support $\Sigma$ is the image of a smooth embedding $\iota:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M^\circ$ from a manifold without boundary, with closed image in the interior $M^\circ$.

A **group-like $p$-form global symmetry** of $\mathcal T$ consists of a locally compact Hausdorff topological group $G$, required to be Abelian when $p>0$, and an assignment $g\mapsto U_g(\Sigma)$ of invertible topological symmetry defects to the allowed closed supports $\Sigma$ of dimension $d-p-1$ and codimension $p+1$. For every support and every ordered pair $g,h\in G$, the model supplies parallel fusion $\star$ and the fusion is defined, with

$$U_e(\Sigma)=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T},\qquad U_g(\Sigma)\star U_h(\Sigma)=U_{gh}(\Sigma),\qquad U_g(\Sigma)\star U_{g^{-1}}(\Sigma)=U_{g^{-1}}(\Sigma)\star U_g(\Sigma)=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T}.$$

Crossing $U_g$ induces a bijection $\rho_g$ on the model's complete typed insertion data, including other defects and their decorations, and a bijection $b\mapsto\beta_g(b)$ on the admissible combined background and boundary data. Both preserve types, supports, algebraic relations and admissibility. With $I$ any complete insertion list and $C_{\mathcal T}$ its model-supplied correlator, covariance means

$$
C_{\mathcal T}(\beta_g(b);\rho_g(I))=C_{\mathcal T}(b;I).
$$

This includes lists with any model-admitted decorated networks, not only ordinary observables. The model specifies crossing junctions and label transport on that domain. Use the convention that crossing $U_g\star U_h$ means crossing $U_h$ and then $U_g$; fusion-action compatibility is the group-action law $\rho_e=\mathrm{id}$, $\rho_{gh}=\rho_g\circ\rho_h$, $\beta_e=\mathrm{id}$ and $\beta_{gh}=\beta_g\circ\beta_h$. The group $G$ is **effective**: if two elements induce identical crossing automorphisms on every admitted observable and background and give identical actions in every admitted correlator, then they are equal. A group element labels a transformation, not the charge of an observable.

The positive-form restriction selects ordinary local invertible symmetry defects: in codimension at least two, two nearby parallel defects can exchange order in a transverse disk while avoiding other insertions. When decorated transport identifies their crossing and background actions, topologicality and fusion identify the actions of $gh$ and $hg$, and effectiveness gives $gh=hg$. This is the local exchange argument; it does not assert that arbitrary wrapped supports or networks on a topologically nontrivial spacetime can be exchanged. In particular, electric and magnetic flux operators constructed from networks with charged junctions can have a mixed commutator on torsion cycles without changing either ordinary local Abelian label group. Such global network operations are not silently included as a non-Abelian positive-form group in this definition. At $p=0$ no Abelian restriction is imposed.

A **genuine $p$-dimensional observable** is an observable supported on a closed embedded $p$-dimensional submanifold whose definition is independent of an attached higher-dimensional support. Its symmetry action is defined by moving a symmetry defect across it, with the model specifying the resulting junction or operator action. For $p>0$, if crossing by every $U_g$ preserves the one-dimensional space $\mathbb C O$ for a nonzero genuine observable $O$, write the scalar action as $\chi_O(g)O$. If the resulting map $\chi_O:G\to U(1)$ is a continuous homomorphism in a model where $G$ is Abelian, call $\chi_O$ the character charge of $O$; it is an element of $\widehat G$. This definition does not assert scalarity, continuity or multiplicativity for every observable. For $p=0$, local observables may carry higher-dimensional representations of a non-Abelian group; the representation label is distinct from the group element implementing a transformation. For a locally compact Hausdorff Abelian group $A$, write its character group as $\widehat A=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cts}}(A,U(1))$, with pointwise multiplication. Here $U(1)=\{e^{i\alpha}:\alpha\in\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z\}$, so every character value and its argument are dimensionless.

A **background** for a symmetry is nondynamical model data, not summed over. For a finite Abelian group $A$, fix a triangulation $K$ of $M$ and let $C^k(K;A)$ be the group of functions from oriented $k$-simplices to $A$, with orientation reversal acting by negation. Its coboundary is the alternating sum over faces,

$$
(\delta c)([v_0,\ldots,v_{k+1}])=\sum_{j=0}^{k+1}(-1)^j c([v_0,\ldots,\widehat v_j,\ldots,v_{k+1}]).
$$

Since $\delta^2=0$ by pairwise cancellation of twice-deleted faces, a discrete $(p+1)$-form background with no higher-group mixing is a cocycle $B\in C^{p+1}(K;A)$ modulo $B\mapsto B+\delta\Lambda$ for $\Lambda\in C^p(K;A)$. Relative cochains or boundary-fixed gauge transformations are used when required by the model's boundary conditions. If other backgrounds mix with $B$, the model must give the modified cocycle and gauge-transformation laws.

For a continuous $U(1)^r$ $p$-form symmetry, use the following global differential-character model. For $k\geq0$, let $C_k^\infty(M;\mathbb Z)$ be the abelian group of finite integer sums of restrictions to the standard oriented $k$-simplex of smooth maps defined on a neighborhood of that simplex, with boundary the alternating sum of face maps, and let $Z_k^\infty(M;\mathbb Z)=\ker\partial$. For a smooth $k$-form $\omega$, set $\int_c\omega=\sum_\sigma n_\sigma\int_{\Delta^k}\sigma^*\omega$ when $c=\sum_\sigma n_\sigma\sigma$. A normalized degree-$(p+2)$ $U(1)$ differential character is a pair $(\check b,H)$ consisting of a group homomorphism $\check b:Z_{p+1}^\infty(M;\mathbb Z)\to U(1)$ and a smooth closed real $(p+2)$-form $H$ such that

$$\check b(\partial c)=\exp\!\left(i\int_c H\right)\quad\text{for every }c\in C_{p+2}^\infty(M;\mathbb Z).$$

Indeed, taking $c=z$ for a cycle $z$ gives $\check b(0)=1=\exp(i\int_zH)$, so $\int_zH\in2\pi\mathbb Z$. A $U(1)^r$ background is an $r$-tuple of such characters and curvatures. The character records holonomy on every smooth integral $(p+1)$-cycle, including flat holonomy data that the curvature alone does not record. An optional local presentation on a contractible $V\subset M$ is a smooth potential $B_V\in\Omega^{p+1}(V)$ with $dB_V=H|_V$ and with character values on cycles $z$ in $V$ given by $\check b(z)=\exp(i\int_zB_V)$. The global pair is the background datum, so no choice of local overlap or lower-overlap variables is additional model data; local presentations represent the same background exactly when they specify the same pair $(\check b,H)$. In a global-potential presentation $B\in\Omega^{p+1}(M)$ with $H=dB$, this includes small transformations $B\mapsto B+d\Lambda$ for smooth $p$-forms $\Lambda$ and large shifts $B\mapsto B+\eta$ by smooth closed $(p+1)$-forms $\eta$ whose periods are in $2\pi\mathbb Z$; for nontrivial sectors the equality-of-pair rule is the complete gauge-equivalence condition. If fixed boundary data are imposed, the selected model specifies the corresponding relative chain and character convention. The unit system and all coefficients in background couplings remain model inputs. The model must define its correlators in these backgrounds; this definition asserts neither that every symmetry admits such a coupling nor that the symmetry can be gauged.
items.physical_scope: A kinematic definition for a named d-dimensional model with model-defined fields, correlators, symmetry defects and background sectors; it asserts no continuum QFT existence, anomaly absence, universal background coupling, or gauging.

items.title: Exchangeability makes p-form symmetry groups Abelian and simple charges characters
items.design_state: Complete conditional proof authored; its p-form definition prerequisite is current and ready.
items.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, $1\le p<d$, and let $\mathcal T$ be a selected model with the following raw group-like defect data. Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff topological group, with no Abelianity assumption. On every admitted closed codimension-$(p+1)$ support, supply invertible topological endodefects $U_g$ with total parallel fusion $U_g\star U_h=U_{gh}$, transparent identity and inverses. Supply crossing bijections $\rho_g$ on complete typed insertion data and background/boundary bijections $\beta_g$, preserving types, supports, algebraic relations and admissibility, with $\rho_{gh}=\rho_g\circ\rho_h$, $\beta_{gh}=\beta_g\circ\beta_h$ and identity actions at $e$. Require covariance $C_{\mathcal T}(\beta_g(b);\rho_g(I))=C_{\mathcal T}(b;I)$ for every complete admitted insertion list $I$ and background $b$, including decorated networks, and invariance of each declared correlator under admissible isotopies transporting all defect data. Require effectiveness: equal crossing actions on the complete domain, equal background maps, and equal actions in all admitted correlators imply equal group labels. These are the model, topologicality, fusion, crossing, covariance and effectiveness data of the preceding symmetry definition, with its extra positive-form Abelianity restriction deliberately withheld. Suppose that for every $g,h\in G$ and every allowed configuration of remaining insertions and fixed data, the model admits two parallel copies of their codimension-$(p+1)$ symmetry supports inside a contractible neighborhood with a disk spanned by two independent normal directions, and an admissible isotopy exchanging their order without intersecting any other insertion or changing boundary or model data. Require that the model-supplied transport along this isotopy identifies the two composite crossing bijections on all complete typed insertion data and the two composite background maps; that is, it identifies $\rho_g\circ\rho_h$ with $\rho_h\circ\rho_g$ and $\beta_g\circ\beta_h$ with $\beta_h\circ\beta_g$. Then $G$ is Abelian, so these data satisfy also the positive-form group restriction in that definition.

For the separate character conclusion, assume additionally that the crossing action has a unitary Hilbert-space realization: there are a complex Hilbert space $\mathcal H$ and a group homomorphism $V:G\to U(\mathcal H)$, with $V_e=I$ and $V_{gh}=V_gV_h$, such that crossing $U_g$ acts on bounded linear operators by $O\mapsto V_gOV_g^{-1}$. Let $O\in B(\mathcal H)$ be a nonzero genuine $p$-dimensional operator, where $B(\mathcal H)$ is the space of bounded linear operators with norm $\|O\|:=\sup_{\|\psi\|=1}\|O\psi\|<\infty$. Call $O$ **simple for this result** if crossing each $U_g$ sends it to a scalar multiple $\chi_O(g)O$, and assume the map $g\mapsto\chi_O(g)\in\mathbb C$ is continuous. Then $\chi_O:G\to U(1)$ is a continuous character, so the charge of $O$ belongs to the Pontryagin dual $\widehat G=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,U(1))$. Neither conclusion is asserted for $p=0$; the character conclusion also makes no claim for nonscalar crossing actions.
items.physical_scope: The group-Abelianity conclusion uses total group-like fusion, effectiveness, the stated local exchange isotopies, and model transport identifying the composite crossing and background maps; the separate character conclusion assumes a unitary Hilbert-space crossing action and a nonzero bounded simple operator with continuous scalar action.

title: Higher-Form Symmetries and Charge Operators — Examples

items.title: Magnetic one-form charge of an external U(1) line
items.design_state: The field-configuration proof derives the U(1) character directly from the integer flux data, so it does not import the abstract theorem or assume that the line satisfies its Hilbert-space simplicity hypotheses.
items.statement:
Use natural units $\hbar=c=1$ and $M=\mathbb R^4$ with its standard orientation and Euclidean metric. Let $C$ be an admitted closed smooth oriented curve and set $X=M\setminus C$. The selected field model is pure compact Maxwell theory with actual gauge group $U(1)=\{e^{i\alpha}:\alpha\in\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z\}$, no dynamical electric or magnetic matter, and an ordinary smooth right principal $U(1)$-bundle $P\to X$ with smooth connection, using the defining character and the standard compact-circle normalization. The model admits nonzero genuine external magnetic line probes $T_n(C')$ for every $n\in\mathbb Z$ on its admitted closed smooth oriented curves $C'$, with flux $2\pi n$ on sufficiently small linking spheres; in each correlator sector considered below, one such line is fixed and is the only magnetic source. In particular, the complete admitted insertion data include a unit-charge probe $T_1$, which is used to make the $U(1)$ symmetry action effective. A principal connection is a smooth $\mathfrak u(1)$-valued one-form reproducing each fundamental vertical vector and equivariant under the right group action. Identify $\mathfrak u(1)=i\mathbb R$ with $\mathbb R$ by $ia\mapsto a$, so its local potentials $A_i$ have holonomy $\exp(i\int A_i)$ and the real curvature $F$ obeys $F|_{U_i}=dA_i$, since the Abelian Lie bracket vanishes. The model fixes the action convention $S[A]=(2e^2)^{-1}\int F\wedge *F$ with dimensionless $e>0$, integrating outside any prescribed line-core tube with its declared boundary condition. It also fixes the allowed bundle sectors, boundary behavior at infinity, and any regulator or measure; no continuum measure is constructed here. With this normalization $[A_i]=\mathrm{length}^{-1}$, $[F]=\mathrm{length}^{-2}$, and $\int_\Sigma F$ is dimensionless.

Let $C$ be the closed image of an orientation-preserving smooth embedding $c:\mathcal C\hookrightarrow M$ from an oriented smooth one-manifold $\mathcal C$ without boundary, and in the sector being calculated let it carry the admitted genuine external magnetic line $T_m(C)$, where genuine means that no auxiliary surface is attached to define the insertion. At each $x\in C$, orient the normal quotient $N_xC:=T_xM/T_xC$ by requiring that a positive tangent $u\in T_xC$, followed by lifts of a positive basis of $N_xC$, gives the positive orientation of $T_xM$. Orient every small linking sphere $S^2_{\mathrm{link}}$ as the boundary of a small ball in $N_xC$, with the outward normal first. The line's integer charge $m\in\mathbb Z$ is specified by $\int_{S^2_{\mathrm{link}}}F=2\pi m$ on every sufficiently small such sphere. In this sector the model has no other magnetic source. Its complete input domain for this fixed sector has the external line $T_m(C)$, any finite list of compact oriented surface insertions $U_{\alpha_j}(\Sigma_j)$ disjoint from $C$, and any finite list of admitted gauge-invariant ordinary field functionals $f_k$ with specified supports. The data $b$ record the boundary behavior at infinity, any excised core-tube boundary condition, bundle sectors and regulator choices. Let $\mathscr F_{C,m,b}$ be the complex vector space of actual functions on the admitted bundle-and-connection configurations generated by finite products of these $f_k$ and the surface functions defined below, with equality understood pointwise. The selected model supplies a complex-linear functional $\mathcal L_{C,m,b}$ on that space, with its prescribed normalization. Its complete correlator rule is

$$
C_b(T_m(C);U_{\alpha_1}(\Sigma_1),\ldots,U_{\alpha_r}(\Sigma_r);f_1,\ldots,f_n)=\mathcal L_{C,m,b}\!\left(\prod_{j=1}^rU_{\alpha_j}(\Sigma_j)\prod_{k=1}^nf_k\right).
$$

There is no assumption that $\mathcal L_{C,m,b}(1)$ is nonzero. The functional, admissibility and normalization are conditional model inputs; no continuum measure is constructed. Gauge changes transport configurations and $b$, with the model's functional required to satisfy the corresponding pullback covariance. Allowed support isotopies transport all orientations and line boundary data, keep $b$ fixed, and avoid the other insertions. Pointwise equalities of the displayed functions therefore imply equalities for every such complete correlator by linearity, and a constant pointwise phase factors out of it.

For a compact smooth oriented two-manifold $\Sigma$ without boundary and a smooth embedding $\iota:\Sigma\hookrightarrow X$, and $\alpha\in\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$, define the magnetic surface operator using any representative $\widetilde\alpha\in\mathbb R$:

$$
U_\alpha(\Sigma)=\exp\!\left(\frac{i\widetilde\alpha}{2\pi}\int_\Sigma F\right).
$$

For this example, a smooth singular three-chain is a finite integer linear combination of smooth maps from the standard 3-simplex, with boundary the alternating sum of its face maps. For a source-free move, the model supplies a compact smooth singular three-chain $V$ in $M\setminus C$ with $\partial V=\Sigma_1-\Sigma_0$. For a move across the line, the model supplies a compact oriented smooth three-dimensional track $W$ in $M$, represented as a finite smooth singular chain, with endpoint boundary $\partial W=\Sigma_1-\Sigma_0$; its support is a smooth embedded three-manifold near each of its finitely many intersections with $C$, and the intersections are transverse interior points. Transverse means that the tangent space of this three-manifold and the tangent line of $C$ span $T_xM$. At an intersection $x_j$, let $u$ be a positive tangent vector to $C$ and $(w_1,w_2,w_3)$ a positive basis of $T_{x_j}W$. Set $\epsilon_j=+1$ when $(u,w_1,w_2,w_3)$ is positive in $T_{x_j}M$ and $\epsilon_j=-1$ otherwise; this ordered convention defines $I(W,C):=\sum_j\epsilon_j$. The quotient map $T_{x_j}W\to N_{x_j}C$ then has orientation sign $\epsilon_j$. Orient each small linking sphere $S_j^2$ as the boundary of a small ball in the already oriented normal space, with the outward normal first. Since the inner boundary of the punctured track has the opposite boundary orientation, excising a small open three-ball at each intersection gives a punctured chain $V$ in $M\setminus C$ with $\partial V=\Sigma_1-\Sigma_0-\sum_j\epsilon_jS_j^2$. The claimed action is that a source-free move leaves $U_\alpha$ unchanged, while a move across the line multiplies it by $e^{i\widetilde\alpha m I(W,C)}$. In particular, the line carries the character $\chi_m(e^{i\alpha})=e^{i\alpha m}$ of the magnetic one-form $U(1)$ symmetry.
items.physical_scope: A conditional field-configuration example for a pure compact U(1) Maxwell model in four Euclidean dimensions with an external genuine magnetic line; it makes no continuum-measure, empirical, or general interacting-QFT claim.

items.title: A non-Abelian zero-form symmetry and its representation labels
items.design_state: Complete finite-model verification authored; the p-form and character-theorem suppliers are current and ready.
items.statement:
Let $M=S^1_\beta$ be Euclidean time of circumference $\beta>0$, let $\mathcal H=\mathbb C^3$ with orthonormal basis $e_1,e_2,e_3$, and let the Hamiltonian be $H_0=0$. Use natural units $\hbar=1$. The finite model's normalized correlation functional for time-ordered operator insertions is $C(O_1,\ldots,O_n)=\frac13\operatorname{Tr}(O_1\cdots O_n)$. Let $S_3$ be the group of permutations of $\{1,2,3\}$, with composition $(\sigma\tau)(j)=\sigma(\tau(j))$, and define the unitary action $\rho(\sigma)e_j=e_{\sigma(j)}$. A symmetry defect at time $t$ is $U_\sigma(t)=\rho(\sigma)$. The complete admissible inputs are arbitrary finite lists of distinct points in a fixed cyclic time order, each carrying either an ordinary matrix $O\in\operatorname{End}(\mathbb C^3)$ or a defect matrix $U_\sigma$, with the same ordered product and normalized trace rule for every such mixed list. The circle has no boundary and this model has no varying background, so its combined background/boundary-data set is a singleton. The value space is $\mathbb C$ with its usual topology. A symmetry $g$ conjugates every insertion matrix by $\rho(g)$, sends a defect label $\sigma$ to $g\sigma g^{-1}$, and fixes the singleton background datum. These are bijections of the complete input domain.

The state space decomposes as $\mathcal H=\mathbb C(e_1+e_2+e_3)\oplus V_2$, where $V_2=\{(z_1,z_2,z_3)\in\mathbb C^3:z_1+z_2+z_3=0\}$. The first summand is the trivial representation and $V_2$ is the two-dimensional standard irreducible representation. The representation label of a state sector is therefore either the trivial representation or the standard two-dimensional representation; a permutation $\sigma\in S_3$ is instead a group element implementing a symmetry transformation. This is an ordinary $p=0$ example and does not conflict with the exchange theorem for $p\ge1$.
items.physical_scope: A finite three-state quantum-mechanical system with a unitary S3 zero-form symmetry; the representation decomposition is exact for this finite model and makes no field-theory or empirical claim.
